'''Willem van der Woude''' (15 January 1876 – 23 September 1974) was a Dutch mathematician and [[rector (academia)|''rector magnificus'']] (chancellor) of the [[University of Leiden]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Bertin, E.|author2=Bos, H.|author3=Grootendorst, A.|title=Two decades of mathematics in the Netherlands 1920–1940|publisher=Mathematical Centre, Amsterdam|year=1978}}</ref>

==Education and career==
[[File:WvdWoude1945.jpg|thumb|left|Van der Woude (middle) as rector in Leiden (1945)]]
Van der Woude studied at the [[University of Groningen]], and subsequently, from 1901 to 1916, worked as a secondary school teacher in [[Deventer]]. In 1908 he received his Ph.D. from the University of Groningen under [[Pieter Hendrik Schoute]] with a thesis titled ''Over elkaar snijdende normalen aan een ellipsoide en een hyperellipsoide''<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=49685}}</ref> (On intersecting normals to an [[ellipsoid]] and a hyperellipsoid). From 1916 until his retirement as professor emeritus in 1947 he was professor of mathematics and mechanics at the University of Leiden.

In 1924, he was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Toronto.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897, International Mathematical Union (IMU) |access-date=2015-09-23 |archive-date=2017-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> In the years 1923, 1924, 1939 and 1940 he chaired the [[Royal Dutch Mathematical Society]].

He acted as ''rector magnificus'' of the University of Leiden during three separate periods: 1934–1935, 1941–43 and 1945 (until he was succeeded by [[Berend George Escher]]).

==Selected publications==
* {{cite book|title=Over 't snijpuntenstelsel van twee algebraïsche krommen|publisher=Noordhoff|year=1916}} (On the intersection system of two algebraic curves)
* {{cite book|title=Meetkunde en ruimteleer|publisher=Stenfert Kroese|year=1935}} (On geometry and theories of space)
